caption:
Figure 2: MERLIN Overview. The context is split into segments Ci (middle row). Each segment
stores a memory state (top row) and the first and second moments of its keys (bottom row). At po-
sition t, the query qt reads segment-level outputs from memory states (step 1). The query computes
the mean and variance of the key-query alignment from the moments (step 2). The final output is
a weighted sum of segment-level outputs, where the weights are derived from a gated mix of the
alignment mean and variance (step 3).
